Jordan — thanks for the clear context and the forecast. Quick summary of options that map to what you asked: 

1) Top-up (add GPUs to same reserved pool, prorated billing to the end of current commitment)
   - Pricing: list price for additional GPUs prorated, with eligibility for a one-time mid-term commitment discount when total commit increases.
   - Typical discount: 7–12% off list for mid-term add if total commit increases by >=25% and you agree to extend the term to align with a 12-month rolling commit.
   - SLA/Throughput: no change to standard per-token SLOs; throughput scales linearly with added GPUs. We will size continuous batching and routing to preserve 99th pct latency target.

2) Exchange (reclassify existing burst usage as reserved + additional top-up)
   - Pricing: larger uplift may unlock better tiered pricing (12–18% depending on final commit).
   - Operational: requires a short service window to reassign capacity and update routing policies (typically <2 hours, scheduled).

3) Short-duration addon (7-month term for exactly 3 GPUs)
   - Pricing: premium vs full commit (roughly +15% on per-GPU price) because shorter term.

Recommendation: given your forecast (spike for 7 months and sustained growth), Option 1 with a 12-month extension on the combined commit gives the best unit economics. I attached a preliminary quote with three scenarios (pro-rata top-up, exchange with 12% discount, short addon).
